steps.text: Combine canola oil, root beer, Worcestershire sauce, teriyaki sauce, steak sauce, garlic salt, onion salt, black pepper, basil, thyme, and rosemary in a bowl.

Pierce steaks in several places on both sides with a fork or knife tip; transfer to a shallow glass or ceramic non-reactive dish in a single layer. Pour marinade over steaks, flip to evenly coat. Cover the dish with plastic wrap and marinate in the refrigerator, 3 to 4 hours, flipping steaks halfway through.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat and lightly oil the grate.
Remove steaks from marinade and shake off excess. Discard remaining marinade.

Cook steaks on the preheated grill until beginning to firm and slightly pink in centers, 5 to 7 minutes per side. An instant-read thermometer inserted into centers should read 140 degrees F (60 degrees C) for medium.

raw_recipe.headline: Juicy Marinated Steaks
raw_recipe.description: This recipe for juicy marinated steaks delivers hints of acidity, sweetness, herbs, and spices without overwhelming the robust flavor of a good steak.

review.reviewBody: good marinade-however anyone that cooks meat knows you don't pierce meat prior to cooking as it makes the meat give off the juices while cooking. And let the meat rest after cooking to allow meat to redistribute the juices contained inside the meat.

Great, with changes. Celery salt and garlic salt add way too much sodium to the end product; I added fresh minced garlic and all fresh herbs instead, and used a low sodium teriyaki sauce. If you pierce the steak in a few places and let the marinade soak in for a few hours or overnight, the meat should still grill up nicely. It is VERY important to let the meat come to room temperature before grilling (at least 30 mins to an hour outside the fridge) before cooking, and let it rest for at least 5 mins when finished grilling before cutting/serving the steaks so the juices can redistribute rather than just running out all over the plate.
Try putting it in a ziplock bag. Squeeze all the air out. That way you don't have to pierce the meat. If you have a vacuum sealer even better. Leave marinate over night.
Never marinate a high quality cut of beef. Salt and pepper is all you need. Now, if it is a skirt or tri-tip, then do so.

i used soy sauce instead of teriyaki because that is what i had. i also used coke because i had no root beer. the garlic and onion salt i switched for powder. on the herbs i used oregano, red pepper flakes, cayenne. i also chopped up a jalapeno pepper, garlic cloves and red onions because i was making tacos. i had thin cut eye of round steaks and we know how tough those can be. i marinated for 2 days and oh my! i cooked them in a cast iron skillet until done all the way thru and they were so tender i couldn't believe it! made awesome steak tacos! i will try the original recipe when i get all my supplies stocked. this is a awesome marinade that i will go to again and again for those tougher cuts of meat. i also like that you can change up your herbs and spices to suit your taste or the cuisine you are having. thanks denis!
I eliminated the salt and used granulated garlic and onion powder instead of garlic salt and onion salt. There is plenty of salt in some of the other ingredients. Very tasty!!

I didn't use high-quality root beer, just whatever I could find. Also used a heaping spoonful of minced garlic in place of the garlic salt and fresh herbs instead of dried.

It was amazing! Made the meat super tender and juicy. Flavor wasn't overpowering but added just enough to make the entire table say, "mmmmmmmm!" at the first bite. 

Great marinade!
1"thick Strip steak. next, Weber ( hot ash), cook 3 to 4 min a side. Rest and serve.

NEVER, EVER pierce a tender steak like a rib eye at any time before, during, or after the cooking process! There won't be a bit of natural juices left. This recipe is great for a flank steak or London broil because those steaks need help with juiciness and tenderness. I gave it three stars instead of five stars because of the advice to pierce the rib eyes.

I seldom marinate a quality steak but when I do, I do pierce the steak with a fork to allow the marinade to do it's work and I have never had a steak lose it's juices or dry out when poked PRIOR to cooking. And I have grilled many, many great steaks in my life. One hint: For perfect medium-rare steaks, grill for 10 minutes per inch -- 2 minutes on the first side and the remaining time on the other side.
REALLY GREAT. This marinade made the juiciest steak. Very flavorful. I did not pierce steak ahead of time, and only had 2 hours to marinade. I used coke. This will be used many times.
Nicely marinated

Giving this a five-star rating, becuse I love al of the ingredients, not because I have made it. Question: Can I broil this steak instead of grilling? In Florida, it's 4 thousand degrees outside and 900% humidity...not good for the BBQ! If broiling, do I sear the steak first? How long under the broiler? Thanks, everyone for all the wonderful tips!
This is a very good marinade! Will definitely use it again, as well as put it in my kitchen book
This was very flavorful. It was different and will definitely add this to my list of favorites.
Fabulous!!!!!!
The marinade was not as good as I read about. My personal taste buds did not get impressed. I followed the directions and marinaded it be for 4 days.
I will definately make it again. Had some friends over to share and got nothing but compliments. And empty plates. That recipe is a keeper.

I did double the recipe...extremely flavorful and tender....I used it on New York strip steaks....I did not have the steak sauce so I omitted it.....excellent! Will use for any beef and I want to try it on pork chops...
These were the best steaks! The marinade was excellent. Everyone who loves steak should try this recipe.
